{{DISPLAYTITLE:''n''-category number}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''category number''' of a [[mathematician]] is a humorous construct invented by [[Dan Freed]],<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Freed|first1=Dan|title=The Verlinde Algebra is Twisted Equivariant K-Theory|journal=Turkish Journal of Mathematics|date=2001|volume=25|issue=1|pages=159–167|arxiv=math/0101038 |bibcode=2001math......1038F }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Freed|first1=Dan|url=https://www.ma.utexas.edu/users/dafr/MSRI_25.pdf|title=Remarks on Chern-Simons Theory|accessdate=8 August 2016}}</ref>
intended to measure the capacity of that mathematician to stomach the use of [[higher category theory|higher categories]]. It is defined as the largest number ''n'' such that they can think about ''n''-categories for a half hour without getting a splitting headache.
